prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: first-person point-and-click western fantasy castle game environment. Generate ONE finished landscape 1536x1024 image, 3:2, full bleed, no collage. This is the NEW INNER COURTYARD of an inhabited western fantasy LORD'S CASTLE. Fine realistic environmental painting, richly tactile warm-gray limestone ashlar, restrained pointed stone detailing, charcoal-slate roofs, dark oak and small aged bronze fittings; natural daylight, cared-for surroundings, crisp coherent architecture. It belongs to the same castle as a private walled rose garden, dignified great hall and oak-furnished stone interiors.
PRIMARY REQUEST: unmistakably a substantial lord's CASTLE enclosing a broad, spacious inner court. Its architectural mass and generous courtyard scale must be clear immediately. Build an appreciably larger and more imposing court than a cozy residential quadrangle: approximately 32 metres across and 42 metres deep as a compositional guide, traversing it feels like a walk of several dozen paces. This is a prosperous inhabited castle, with imposing stone structure, not a small manor house or rows of village houses. Avoid turning it into a giant imperial palace or a military parade ground.
VIEWPOINT: first-person, standing on the courtyard paving at 1.65 metres eye height immediately outside the great hall entrance. Camera optical axis horizontal, looking diagonally across the open court so one side recedes with convincing depth. The great hall doorway is BEHIND the viewer and is not visible. A short substantial stone corner or deeply projecting buttress of the hall may frame the extreme foreground edge. Natural 32-35mm lens, not a fisheye or panoramic lens; absolutely no aerial view, elevated balcony, high terrace, looking down or architectural cutaway. Establish scale through building depth, receding paving and a small well, without people.
CASTLE MASSING: long substantial TWO-STOREY limestone wings have tall storeys, strongly continuous masonry, thick walls, deeply recessed arched windows and solid buttressed corners. Keep the existing castle's two-storey residential-wing arrangement but give the walls dignified height and weight. A robust round crenellated corner tower rises clearly above a wing and shows a substantial continuous stone shaft integrated into the walls, not merely a tiny decorative turret peeking above roofs. The enclosing walls and tower dominate the upper two-thirds of the image. Dark slate roofs form quiet unified roof planes set above the broad high stone elevations; minimize tiny dormers, little gables, cottage chimneys and exposed timber eaves. Restrained heavy stone corbels and deeply shaded window embrasures communicate castle construction. Warm domestic hints may appear within a few windows, but the overall architecture must be fortified stone, not a domestic townhouse facade. Window proportions remain believable and provide scale; do not multiply many floors or make it a cathedral.
COURTYARD: an expansive uninterrupted field of subtly worn limestone flagstones stretches across the foreground and middle, with generous lateral breathing room and obvious depth to the opposite wing. Side wings are spaced far enough apart for a carriage to turn comfortably, though no carriage or horse is present. Keep the far wall meaningfully distant rather than right in front of the camera. A plain small stone well, with a simple iron hoisting support and no miniature house-like roof, stands off to the LEFT mid-distance near a wall; the well occupies little of the frame and helps communicate the size of the court. A few sparse climbing plants and a single planted stone urn are confined to wall edges. Keep the middle clear, no flower-bed garden in the court and no clutter. Natural building shadows break up the pavement without darkness hiding details.
ONE VISIBLE EXIT: at the RIGHT side in accessible middle distance, in a connecting lower stone wall, place one broad open pointed pale-limestone GARDEN GATE with two restrained moulded stone arch bands, complete side jambs and visible threshold. Through it glimpse lush climbing roses in creamy white and soft pink, leafy shrubs and a short pale-stone garden path at the SAME GROUND LEVEL. An iron gate leaf is folded flat inside the wall and does not cover the opening. This should be unmistakable and large enough to click, but must not occupy a huge portion of the image or force the opposite wing to seem close. All other visible openings are clearly glazed windows, not additional doors. The great hall return is behind the camera. No further navigable doorways, arcades, tunnels, exterior gatehouses or branching destinations.
LIGHT AND MOOD: bright gentle afternoon daylight, pale blue sky, varied soft shadows, sunlight catching weathered stone edges, quiet nobility and restrained inhabited warmth. The picture should feel physically grounded, substantial and welcoming, with rich natural material texture. No figures, soldiers, people, animals, text, flags, heraldic emblems, named symbols, UI, arrows, hotspot outlines, return-door icon, watermark, modern objects, distant towns or new geographical landmarks.
